User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the Lazywear e-commerce platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

email.description: Email address of the user. Optional for phone auth.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a product available for sale on the Lazywear platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product entity.

price.description: Price of the product in INR.

imageUrl.description: URL of the product's main image.

categoryIds.description: References to Categories. (Relationship: Category N:N Product)

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a category of products on the Lazywear platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the category entity.

name.description: Name of the category (e.g., Shirts, Pants, Shoes).

Order.title: Order
Order.description: Represents an order placed by a user on the Lazywear platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the order entity.

orderDate.description: Date when the order was placed.

status.description: Status of the order (e.g., pending, processing, shipped, delivered).

OrderItem.title: OrderItem
OrderItem.description: Represents an item within an order.

id.description: Unique identifier for the order item entity.

quantity.description: Quantity of the product in the order item.

price.description: Price of the product at the time of order.

Wishlist.title: Wishlist
Wishlist.description: Represents a user's wishlist of products.

id.description: Unique identifier for the wishlist entity.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support the Lazywear e-commerce platform, focusing on product catalog, user management, orders, and wishlists. The design emphasizes authorization independence via denormalization, making security rules simple and efficient. It uses hierarchical paths for user-owned data and membership maps for collaborative access where applicable.  

Authorization Independence is achieved primarily by avoiding `get()` calls in security rules. For instance, user-specific data like orders and wishlists are stored under `/users/{userId}`, so rules can authorize based on `request.auth.uid == userId` without needing to fetch user data. The `Order` collection includes the `userId` to associate it with a specific user. This structure avoids hierarchical authorization dependencies, ensuring atomic operations.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters) are supported through structural segregation. User-specific data is stored under `/users/{userId}`, while global data like products and categories are stored in top-level collections. This separation allows for secure `list` operations. For example, listing products does not require filtering based on user roles because all products are accessible, according to product read rules. Private user data like wishlists can only be accessed by the authenticated user, ensuring data privacy.

Global roles aren't explicitly required in this design, but could be added using an existence-based approach with a `/roles_admin/{uid}` collection. For collaborative data models, a membership map could be employed to control write access to collaborative entities, which aren't present in this design.
